Hi Jordan (and Ava),

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the candid discussion. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Pain points you shared:
- Latency variability on the current shared endpoints during peak hours (~300–600ms increased tail latency).
- Data isolation requirements for PHI and internal models (must be within a customer-dedicated environment).
- Predictable throughput for nightly batch processing and daytime interactive agents.

Goals you highlighted:
- Dedicated GPU pool with strict network isolation (VPC + customer-managed NAT).
- SLA: 99.9% uptime and a 95th percentile token latency target around 150ms for short-form generation.
- Autoscaling to support scheduled nightly batch runs (burst up to 3x baseline).
- Integration timeline target: pilot in Q4, production by end of Q1.

High-level Dedicated recommendation (attached: Redwood_Dedicated_Capacity_Proposal_v1.pdf):
- Reserved capacity: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (pool for inference + KV cache nodes).
- Isolation: dedicated tenant in our Private offering with customer VPC peering + KMS integration.
- Scaling plan: baseline pool sized for steady-state traffic; burst policy using queued capacity and pre-warmed instances for nightly windows. See scaling-plan-diagram.png.
- SLA & support: SLA draft attached (SLA_Draft_AcmeHealth.docx); options for 24/7 on-call support at enterprise tier.

1) Can you confirm the expected RPS and average sequence length for the daytime interactive agent? That will help finalize GPU sizing.
2) Any additional compliance artifacts beyond SOC 2 (e.g., HITRUST) we should prepare for early in the pilot?
3) Who should receive the contract/Procurement thread — legal@acmehealth.com or procurement@acmehealth.com?

Hi Jordan — following up with the technical details you asked for. Short answers first, then a quick table of numbers below.

1) Cold-start latency and pre-warm behavior:
- Cold-start (spin-up new instance + model load): ~45–75s depending on model size and quantization.
- Warm instance (GPU initialized, model in memory, KV cache empty): first-token latency comparable to steady-state once warmed — typically additional 10–20ms overhead.
- Pre-warm strategy: maintain a small pool of pre-warmed replicas during burst windows; pre-warmed nodes reduce cold-start to near-zero for capacity already allocated.

2) Private model uploads & isolation:
- Yes — we support customer-owned model artifacts uploaded to a customer-managed object store and mounted into the Dedicated runtime. All artifacts remain in your VPC (no model weights leave the tenant). We integrate with KMS for key management and offer encryption-in-transit and at-rest.

3) Autoscaling & burst plan (baseline recommendation for 35 RPS peak):
- Baseline pool: 6 inference replicas (sized to sustain daytime SLA with headroom).
- Burst capacity: additional 2–4 pre-warmed GPUs available for scheduled nightly jobs and unexpected spikes (policy can be 2x baseline for short windows).

Estimated numbers (example):
- 35 RPS, avg seq 120 tokens -> approx 4.2M tokens/hr -> recommend 8x A100-equivalent GPU pool for combined interactive + batch headroom (matches Marissa’s proposal).
- 95th P90 token latency target ~150ms achievable with the above + KV caching for common prefixes.
